title: Career Roadmap: Technical Officer (Army / Navy / IAF)

facts.Course: Technical Entry Scheme (TES) / Navy B.Tech Entry / AFCAT Technical

blocks.text: Technical Officer — Army, Navy or Air Force

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Defence, Security & Emergency Services
EDUCATION PATHWAY
10+2 PCM or an eligible engineering degree
The required qualification depends on the chosen service and entry scheme.
CAREER AREA
Military engineering and technology
Equipment, weapons systems, communications, aircraft, ships, vehicles and technical operations.

sections.heading: What does a Technical Officer do?

blocks.text: A Technical Officer in the Indian Armed Forces combines engineering knowledge, leadership, discipline and operational responsibility. The exact duties differ significantly between the Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force.

blocks.label: Indian Army
blocks.text: Technical appointments may involve military equipment, vehicles, communications, electronics, maintenance systems and engineering support.

blocks.label: Indian Navy
blocks.text: Technical officers may work with ship propulsion, electrical systems, weapons and sensors, electronics, communications or naval aviation systems.

blocks.label: Indian Air Force
blocks.text: Technical officers may work with aircraft systems, avionics, radar, communications, engineering maintenance and technical support operations.
The job is not simply an engineering desk role. It involves military training, command responsibilities, strict service standards, teamwork and readiness for operational assignments.
Path A — Army Technical Entry Scheme (TES)
After Class 12

For eligible candidates with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics who meet the current notification's academic and entrance-examination criteria. This is a route toward an Army officer career with technical education and military training.
Path B — Indian Navy engineering entries
Entry depends on scheme

The Navy offers different officer-entry routes, including technical entries and certain graduate-engineering opportunities. Academic discipline, age, gender, medical criteria and selection stages vary by notification.
Path C — AFCAT Technical Branch
Engineering degree

For eligible engineering graduates who meet the Indian Air Force's current technical-branch requirements. Selection typically includes the applicable AFCAT process, service-specific assessment and medical standards.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: These routes are not interchangeable. TES is an Army-specific entry scheme; Navy B.Tech and other Navy technical entries have their own eligibility rules; AFCAT is an Air Force entry route. Some technical appointments are filled through other notifications, so applicants must follow the exact scheme they qualify for.
Stage 1 — Classes 11–12

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Build eligibility and prepare for officer entry

items.text: Study Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM) if targeting a 10+2 technical entry.
Build mathematics and physics problem-solving skills.
Prepare for JEE Main where it is required or used for shortlisting under the chosen entry scheme.
Practise English communication, reasoning, current affairs and general awareness.
Develop physical fitness, discipline and teamwork.
Track official notifications for age limits, academic marks, gender eligibility and application windows.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Meet the academic requirements and apply only to entry schemes for which you qualify.
Stage 2 — Engineering degree, if applying as a graduate

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Build a strong technical profile

items.text: Select an engineering discipline accepted by the target service and branch.
Prioritise mathematics, electronics, electrical systems, mechanics, computing or aerospace subjects according to your discipline.
Maintain the minimum aggregate required by the relevant notification.
Complete practical projects, laboratory work and technical presentations.
Prepare for AFCAT and any applicable technical selection requirements; also review the IAF's GATE-score entry when eligible.
Practise officer-like communication, teamwork, leadership and decision-making.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Complete the qualifying degree and meet the current technical-branch criteria.
Stage 3 — Application and selection

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Demonstrate officer potential

items.text: Submit the application accurately before the official deadline.
Prepare for the applicable written examination or shortlisting method.
Practise for the Services Selection Board (SSB) or Air Force Selection Board (AFSB), as applicable.
Prepare for psychological assessments, group tasks, interviews and officer-like qualities assessments.
Complete the prescribed service medical examination.
Follow the merit list, vacancy rules and joining instructions for the specific entry.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Complete all required selection stages; final selection depends on eligibility, performance, medical fitness, vacancies and merit.
Stage 4 — Military and technical training

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Become a commissioned officer

items.text: Complete the training prescribed for the selected entry and service.
Build military leadership, discipline, physical endurance and operational awareness.
Study service-specific technical equipment and maintenance or operational procedures.
Develop team leadership, decision-making and responsibility for personnel and equipment.
Complete the required professional and technical training before taking up the assigned duties.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Qualify for commissioning and the duties assigned under the relevant service pathway.
The most useful skills depend on whether the candidate targets Army engineering support, Navy technical branches or Air Force aeronautical engineering.

rows.text: Circuits, electrical machines, power systems and fault diagnosis
Analog and digital electronics, sensors and electronic systems
Networking, embedded systems, communications and cybersecurity fundamentals where relevant
Schematics, maintenance manuals, test reports and technical records
Team coordination, planning, responsibility and decision-making
Following technical procedures, safety rules and information-security requirements

blocks.text: Indian Army — Technical entry

items.text: Strengthen PCM fundamentals and prepare for the academic criteria in the latest TES notification.
Learn basic mechanical, electrical and electronics principles.
Practise communication, group discussion, reasoning and leadership exercises.
Understand that an Army technical officer's duties depend on the commissioned arm or service and subsequent appointment.

blocks.text: Indian Navy — Technical officer

items.text: Build foundations in electrical, electronics, mechanical or other relevant engineering areas.
For the 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry route, monitor the official notification for the required PCM performance, JEE Main shortlisting and age criteria.
Learn about ship systems, propulsion support, sensors, communications and engineering maintenance at an introductory level.
Prepare for the applicable SSB process and service medical requirements.

blocks.text: Indian Air Force — Ground Duty (Technical)

items.text: Check which engineering disciplines qualify for Aeronautical Engineer (Mechanical) or Aeronautical Engineer (Electronics).
Prepare for the applicable AFCAT route and review the separate GATE-score entry if eligible.
Build a solid understanding of engineering fundamentals and technical problem-solving.
Practise interview communication and explain engineering projects clearly.

blocks.text: The Indian Air Force announced a GATE-score shortlisting scheme for its Technical Branch in May 2026. AFCAT remains another route, and eligibility requirements for the technical branch remain tied to the applicable notification.

sections.heading: Physical fitness and officer selection preparation

blocks.text: Physical readiness and suitability for military service are important alongside academic performance.

blocks.label: Endurance
blocks.text: Build running and cardiovascular fitness progressively.

blocks.label: Strength
blocks.text: Develop general strength, mobility and core stability.

blocks.label: Teamwork
blocks.text: Participate in sports or group activities that require cooperation.

blocks.label: Communication
blocks.text: Practise speaking clearly, listening actively and presenting ideas.

blocks.label: Awareness
blocks.text: Follow national and international news, science and technology developments, and defence-related public information.

blocks.label: Self-management
blocks.text: Practise time management, consistency and handling pressure.

Medical standards differ between services, branches and entry schemes. Review the official medical requirements before applying, especially for eyesight, hearing, general health and other service-specific criteria. Do not rely on informal fitness benchmarks as a guarantee of medical eligibility.

sections.heading: Projects and activities that can strengthen a technical profile

blocks.text: For engineering graduates, useful projects demonstrate technical competence, initiative and the ability to explain a problem-solving process.

blocks.label: Embedded systems project
blocks.text: Build a microcontroller-based sensor and monitoring system.

blocks.label: Electrical fault-detection project
blocks.text: Simulate fault conditions and document a safe diagnostic process.

blocks.label: Communications project
blocks.text: Develop a basic networking or signal-processing demonstration using permitted equipment.

blocks.label: Mechanical design project
blocks.text: Model a mechanical component and explain its design constraints.

blocks.label: Reliability analysis
blocks.text: Analyse a non-sensitive, publicly documented engineering system and propose a maintenance plan.

blocks.label: Team engineering project
blocks.text: Work with a team to build, test and present a prototype, documenting each person's contribution.
For candidates applying directly after Class 12, academic performance, required entrance tests, selection preparation and eligibility take priority over building a large project portfolio.
Avoid restricted military equipment, classified information or unauthorised access to defence systems.

rows.text: Age, nationality, academic subjects, marks and other notification conditions
Scheme-specific examination, JEE Main criteria or accepted GATE score where applicable
Interviews, group activities, psychological assessments and leadership assessment
Applicable service and branch medical standards
Vacancy availability, merit position and verification of documents
Physical training, military skills, leadership and professional instruction

items.text: Eligible applicant

blocks.text: Meets the entry scheme's academic, age and other eligibility requirements.

items.text: Selected officer cadet / trainee

blocks.text: Completes the prescribed military and professional training.

items.text: Commissioned Technical Officer

blocks.text: Takes up the duties and responsibilities assigned within the relevant service.

items.text: Experienced Technical Officer

blocks.text: Gains operational experience and may take on greater technical, personnel and equipment responsibilities.

items.text: Senior officer / technical leadership appointments

blocks.text: May progress into leadership, specialist or management appointments according to service rules, performance, qualifications and organisational requirements.
Promotion, tenure, permanent or short service commission, and future assignments depend on the applicable service rules and individual circumstances.

A strong candidate for a Technical Officer pathway should aim to demonstrate:

items.text: Academic eligibility for the selected service and entry scheme.
Sound mathematics, science and, where applicable, engineering fundamentals.
Clear communication, teamwork, leadership potential and responsible decision-making.
Physical readiness and compliance with the relevant medical standards.
Consistent preparation for the required examination, SSB or AFSB assessment.
A clear understanding of military life, service obligations and technical responsibilities.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Decide whether to pursue Army TES after Class 12, an Indian Navy technical entry, or the Indian Air Force's Ground Duty (Technical) route after engineering. Then use the latest official notification to build a preparation plan around that specific pathway.
